entries.title: Paytm gets tentative approval to revive its digital wallet, which effectively died after India's central bank canceled Paytm Payments Bank's license in April (Sankalp Phartiyal/Bloomberg)
OpenAI announces ChatGPT Wallet, which lets its dots AI agents make purchases on behalf of users, available to ChatGPT Pro subscribers in the US who are over 18 (Ashley Capoot/CNBC)
Sources: SpaceX laid off ~60 Grok Imagine staffers in the past week, leaving a handful to keep the product alive, as it prioritizes AI coding tools and Grok Bot (The Information)
Scott Bessent says the departments of Treasury, Defense, State were in favor of putting Megaspeed on the entity list for months, but Commerce is in charge (CNBC)
Jensen Huang's biographer says there was a culture of omertà and deference towards Huang inside Nvidia that enabled him to "be his worst self" (Stephen Witt/New York Times)
Amended S-1: Nscale had $5.5B in debt in September, up from $137.4M in June; Nvidia committed $2B of its $3B+ convertible financing; it previously disclosed $1B (Bloomberg)
Jensen Huang's downfall exposes Nvidia's internal politics; source: Huang ran Nvidia as a "feudal system" with his daughter and son-in-law in powerful positions (Financial Times)
Source: at an August 2026 finance meeting, Jensen Huang interrupted Colette Kress' presentation, calling her "a deer in the headlights" and a "reporting CFO" (Wall Street Journal)
South Korea-based DeepX tapes out DX-M2, an edge AI chip to run inference of 100B-parameter LLMs on robots and drones, targeting fall 2027 for mass production (Sally Ward-Foxton/EE Times)
A review of Chinese contracts, disclosures, and other documents identifies $3.2B+ in compute projects built or planned around Nvidia GPUs restricted by the US (Eduardo Baptista/Reuters)
AI server maker xFusion gets approval from the Shenzhen Stock Exchange for a ChiNext IPO; filing: xFusion aims to raise ~$1.2B by issuing up to 220.08M shares (Sangmi Cha/Bloomberg)
OpenAI launches Daybreak Red Team in early access to test web apps for flaws and Daybreak Defense Factory to automate finding, validating, and fixing them (Jessica Lyons/The Register)
Sources: Samsung is in talks to acquire Modine Manufacturing, a US maker of cooling systems for data centers, as soon as in the coming weeks; MOD jumps 30%+ (Bloomberg)
Filing: Nscale says it needs more funding for its 2027 commitments after ordering Nvidia chips for a $45B Anthropic deal, casting doubt on its planned $35B IPO (Financial Times)
Nscale's updated IPO prospectus shows Q3 revenue up 1,344% YoY to $307.5M, up from $140.6M in Q2, and net loss widened to $1.69B, up from $1.02B in Q2 (Jordan Novet/CNBC)
